faq.a: It means time passes quickly and can’t be paused or recovered, so how we use it matters. It’s a reminder to live intentionally, not a reason to panic.

faq.q: Where does the phrase “time is fleeting” come from?
faq.a: The idea goes back to Virgil’s “tempus fugit” (time flies). The English wording is best known from Longfellow’s 1838 poem “A Psalm of Life”: “Art is long, and Time is fleeting.”

faq.q: Is “time is fleeting” from The Rocky Horror Picture Show?
faq.a: The song “The Time Warp” includes the line “time is fleeting, madness takes its toll,” which made the phrase famous in pop culture, but the expression is much older.

faq.q: Why does time feel faster as we get older?
faq.a: Each year is a smaller share of our total life, and adult routines create fewer new memories. When days look alike, the mind compresses them, so time seems to fly.

faq.q: What is the difference between “time is fleeting” and “life is fleeting”?
faq.a: “Time is fleeting” focuses on how fast hours and years pass; “life is fleeting” points to the limits of a whole lifetime and what deserves priority within it.

faq.q: How can I make time feel slower?
faq.a: Add small new experiences to your week, give one daily activity your full attention, mark milestones with rituals, and keep a one-line journal so days don’t blur together.

faq.q: Is “time is fleeting” a negative saying?
faq.a: Not inherently. It can feel like pressure if used to demand constant productivity, but its original intent is closer to encouragement: focus on what matters before the moment passes.
